mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 3 months indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts investor confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 35% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months indicates a robust supply side, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% annually and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals strong consumer demand coupled with a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: strong consumer demand with tight labor market
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS grows by more than 5% annually and UNRATE is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is growing at an annual rate below 2%, it signals a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 over the previous month signals strong labor demand, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the previous quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of the instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 1%.
